title: Hedging and Stance Markers in Norwegian
goal: Use common Norwegian stance markers to express uncertainty, inference, shared assumptions, source doubt, opinion, and informal approximation.

objectives.statement: Use common Norwegian stance markers to express uncertainty, inference, shared assumptions, source doubt, opinion, and informal approximation.

spans.value: Maja and Henrik work at a small cultural centre. They are preparing an outdoor concert, but several details are still uncertain. Notice how they avoid presenting every statement as a definite fact.
Det kommer visstnok rundt to hundre mennesker på lørdag.

blocks.translation: Apparently, around two hundred people are coming on Saturday.

spans.value: Ja, men det blir kanskje færre hvis det regner.

blocks.translation: Yes, but there may be fewer if it rains.

spans.value: Det gjør det nok. Værmeldingen ser ikke særlig lovende ut.

blocks.translation: It probably will. The weather forecast does not look very promising.

spans.value: Vi bør vel bestille et ekstra telt, da?

blocks.translation: We should probably order an extra tent, then, shouldn’t we?

spans.value: Jo, det er vel tryggest. Men teltet koster visst fem tusen kroner.

blocks.translation: Yes, that is probably safest. But the tent apparently costs five thousand kroner.

spans.value: Så mye? Jeg synes det høres dyrt ut.

blocks.translation: That much? I think it sounds expensive.

spans.value: Enig. Vi trenger jo bare et ganske lite telt, sånn til tjue personer.

blocks.translation: Agreed. After all, we only need a fairly small tent, something like one for twenty people.

spans.value: Da kan vi kanskje låne ett av idrettslaget. De har visst flere.

blocks.translation: Then perhaps we can borrow one from the sports club. They apparently have several.

spans.value: Maja and Henrik use several small words and expressions to show how strongly they stand behind what they say. They distinguish reported information from personal opinion, make careful inferences, appeal to shared knowledge, and give approximate numbers. These expressions are called
stance markers
because they show the speaker’s stance toward a statement.
Without them, the conversation would sound much more certain:

no.value: Det kommer to hundre mennesker.

en.value: Two hundred people are coming.

spans.value: With a source-based hedge, Maja makes it clear that the number comes from information she has received:

no.value: Det kommer visstnok rundt to hundre mennesker.

en.value: Apparently, around two hundred people are coming.

spans.value: The second version does not merely provide less information. It tells Henrik how to interpret the claim: the number is reported, and it may not be fully reliable.
The most common general marker of uncertainty is
kanskje
, meaning perhaps, maybe, or possibly.

no.value: Det blir kanskje færre hvis det regner.

en.value: There may be fewer if it rains.

no.value: Hun kommer kanskje senere.

en.value: Perhaps she is coming later.

no.value: Vi kan kanskje flytte konserten inn.

en.value: We could perhaps move the concert indoors.

spans.value: Kanskje does not explain why the speaker is uncertain. The uncertainty might come from missing information, an undecided plan, or simple caution.
Its position can change the sentence structure. When kanskje appears inside the sentence, normal main-clause word order is common:

no.value: Vi kan kanskje låne et telt.

en.value: Perhaps we can borrow a tent.

spans.value: When kanskje begins a main clause, two patterns are accepted:

no.value: Kanskje kan vi låne et telt.

en.value: Perhaps we can borrow a tent.

no.value: Kanskje vi kan låne et telt.

en.value: Perhaps we can borrow a tent.

spans.value: The first pattern uses verb–subject order after fronted kanskje. The second uses sentence-initial kanskje followed by subject–verb order. Both are accepted Bokmål constructions, and the choice can reflect style or emphasis.
Checkpoint: identifying open uncertainty

Return to the concert preparations. Read several short updates about weather, attendance, transport, and equipment. For each update, rewrite one definite claim so that it becomes an open possibility with kanskje.
The prerequisite lesson established three useful stances toward a claim:
jo
treats it as shared,
vel
often leaves room for the listener's uptake, and
nok
presents it as likely. Here those familiar choices become reference points for a broader system.
Compare open possibility with a likely assessment:

no.value: Det regner kanskje på lørdag.

en.value: Perhaps it will rain on Saturday.

no.value: Det regner nok på lørdag.

en.value: It will probably rain on Saturday.

spans.value: Kanskje
leaves rain as one possibility.
Nok

presents rain as the outcome the speaker considers likely; that assessment may rest on evidence, experience, or an ordinary expectation. The next sections add indirect source, personal viewpoint, and approximation, rather than reteaching each particle separately.

sections.title: Reporting uncertain information with visst and visstnok

spans.value: Maja says that the tent costs five thousand kroner, but she does not present herself as the source:

no.value: Teltet koster visst fem tusen kroner.

en.value: The tent apparently costs five thousand kroner.

spans.value: Henrik later says:

no.value: De har visst flere.

en.value: They apparently have several.

spans.value: Visst
can indicate that the speaker has heard or learned something indirectly. It often corresponds to apparently or I understand that. The speaker passes on the information without fully guaranteeing it.

no.value: Kari har visst fått ny jobb.

en.value: Apparently, Kari has got a new job.

no.value: Veien er visst stengt.

en.value: The road is apparently closed.

no.value: De skal visst flytte til Bergen.

en.value: They are apparently going to move to Bergen.

spans.value: Visstnok
also marks reported information and often makes the distance from the claim especially clear. It can suggest reportedly, supposedly, or according to what I have heard.

no.value: Det kommer visstnok rundt to hundre mennesker.

en.value: Apparently, around two hundred people are coming.

no.value: Restauranten er visstnok en av de beste i byen.

en.value: The restaurant is reportedly one of the best in the city.

no.value: Denne bygningen er visstnok over tre hundre år gammel.

en.value: This building is supposedly more than three hundred years old.

spans.value: In many contexts, visst and visstnok are close. Visst is very common in conversational Bokmål, while visstnok can place slightly more emphasis on the reported or unverified nature of the information.
Do not confuse stance-marking visst with
visst
meaning certainly in more formal or fixed uses, or with
viss
meaning certain or particular:

no.value: Det er visst en feil i programmet.

en.value: Apparently, there is an error in the software.

no.value: Under visse forhold fungerer programmet bedre.

en.value: Under certain conditions, the software works better.

spans.value: The first sentence reports uncertain information. In the second, visse is an inflected form of viss and identifies particular conditions.
There is also an important difference between visst and nok:

no.value: Veien er visst stengt.

en.value: Apparently, the road is closed.

no.value: Veien er nok stengt.

en.value: The road is probably closed.

spans.value: With visst, the speaker has apparently received the information from somewhere. With nok, the speaker reaches a likely conclusion, perhaps after seeing a barrier or a line of stationary cars.
Checkpoint: report or inference

Work with short pieces of context. Some should provide an indirect source, such as a colleague’s message, a local rumour, or an online notice. Others should provide observable evidence, such as barriers across a road or a dark, empty building. State the likely situation using a suitable stance marker.

sections.title: Marking personal opinion with synes, mener, and etter min mening

spans.value: Henrik reacts to the price with a personal evaluation:

no.value: Jeg synes det høres dyrt ut.

en.value: I think it sounds expensive.

spans.value: Synes
is common when expressing an opinion, impression, preference, or evaluation.

no.value: Jeg synes planen virker fornuftig.

en.value: I think the plan seems sensible.

no.value: Vi synes konserten var vellykket.

en.value: We think the concert was successful.

no.value: Synes du dette er en god løsning?

en.value: Do you think this is a good solution?

spans.value: By framing the evaluation as personal, synes leaves room for another person to disagree. It is therefore a useful stance marker in discussion.
Mener
can also mean think, but it commonly presents a more considered belief, position, or claim.

no.value: Jeg mener at kommunen bør støtte arrangementet.

en.value: I believe that the municipality should support the event.

no.value: Henrik mener at teltet er for dyrt.

en.value: Henrik believes that the tent is too expensive.

spans.value: Compare:

no.value: Jeg synes lokalet er hyggelig.

en.value: I think the venue is pleasant.

no.value: Jeg mener at lokalet er det beste alternativet.

en.value: I believe that the venue is the best option.

spans.value: The first is a personal impression. The second sounds more like a position that could be supported with reasons.
Etter min mening
means in my opinion. It explicitly labels the statement as the speaker’s view and is useful when contrasting positions.

no.value: Etter min mening bør vi flytte konserten inn.

en.value: In my opinion, we should move the concert indoors.

no.value: Dette er, etter min mening, den sikreste løsningen.

en.value: This is, in my opinion, the safest solution.

spans.value: Do not pile up opinion markers without a reason:
Less natural:
::: callout {variant=warning} Not: Etter min mening synes jeg at planen er god. (In my opinion, I think that the plan is good.) :::
Usually choose one clear frame:

no.value: Etter min mening er planen god.

en.value: In my opinion, the plan is good.

no.value: Jeg synes planen er god.

en.value: I think the plan is good.

spans.value: A stance marker does not automatically make a forceful statement polite. Tone and wording still matter. Compare:

no.value: Dette er en dårlig idé.

en.value: This is a bad idea.

no.value: Jeg synes dette er en dårlig idé.

en.value: I think this is a bad idea.

no.value: Jeg synes kanskje vi bør vurdere en annen løsning.

en.value: I think perhaps we should consider another solution.

spans.value: The final version combines personal opinion and uncertainty to create more room for discussion. It is softer, but its communicative purpose remains clear.
Checkpoint: presenting a view without turning it into fact

Continue the planning meeting. Give Maja and Henrik different reactions to the price, location, expected attendance, and weather plan. Express each reaction as a personal evaluation or considered position.
Several expressions make quantities less exact. In the opening dialogue, Maja says:

no.value: Det kommer visstnok rundt to hundre mennesker.

en.value: Apparently, around two hundred people are coming.

spans.value: Rundt
means around or approximately before numbers and quantities:

no.value: Det tar rundt en halvtime.

en.value: It takes around half an hour.

no.value: Vi trenger rundt femti stoler.

en.value: We need around fifty chairs.

no.value: Billetten koster rundt fire hundre kroner.

en.value: The ticket costs around four hundred kroner.

spans.value: Omtrent
also means approximately and is neutral in register:

no.value: Det kommer omtrent to hundre mennesker.

en.value: Approximately two hundred people are coming.

no.value: Turen er omtrent ti kilometer lang.

en.value: The walk is approximately ten kilometres long.

spans.value: Cirka
, often written
ca.
in practical texts, is another common equivalent:

no.value: Møtet varer cirka én time.

en.value: The meeting lasts about one hour.

spans.value: In informal conversation,
sånn
can introduce a rough example, size, number, or category:

no.value: Vi trenger et telt sånn til tjue personer.

en.value: We need a tent for something like twenty people.

no.value: Det tar sånn fem–ti minutter.

en.value: It takes something like five to ten minutes.

no.value: Hun er sånn rundt tretti.

en.value: She is, like, around thirty.

spans.value: Sånn is conversational and deliberately loose. It is useful when precision is unnecessary, but it can sound vague in formal reports or technical instructions. In those settings, omtrent, cirka, or a precise figure is usually more suitable.
Avoid unnecessary stacking in neutral prose:
Overloaded:
::: callout {variant=warning} Not: Det kommer kanskje sånn cirka rundt to hundre mennesker. (Perhaps something like around two hundred people are coming, in this situation.) :::
Clearer alternatives:

no.value: Det kommer kanskje rundt to hundre mennesker.

en.value: Perhaps around two hundred people are coming.

no.value: Det kommer visstnok cirka to hundre mennesker.

en.value: Apparently, about two hundred people are coming.

spans.value: Multiple markers can be natural when they do different jobs. In the second sentence, visstnok marks uncertainty about the source, while cirka marks approximation of the number. The sentence communicates both: the report is not fully confirmed, and the reported figure is not exact.
Checkpoint: exact, approximate, or informally rough

Use details from an event plan: audience size, ticket price, walking distance, setup time, and tent capacity. Restate each figure with a degree of precision suited to the situation. Include both neutral planning language and informal conversation between Maja and Henrik.
Norwegian speakers often use more than one marker because each contributes different information. The key is to understand the job of each one.

no.value: Det kommer kanskje rundt hundre personer.

en.value: Perhaps around one hundred people are coming.

spans.value: Kanskje marks uncertainty about whether that expectation is correct. Rundt marks the number as approximate.

no.value: De har visst et telt til sånn tretti personer.

en.value: Apparently, they have a tent for something like thirty people.

spans.value: Visst marks indirect information. Sånn makes the capacity informally approximate.

no.value: Vi bør vel kanskje ringe dem først.

en.value: Perhaps we should probably call them first, shouldn’t we?

spans.value: Both vel and kanskje soften the proposal. This combination is possible in conversation, but too many hedges can make a speaker sound hesitant. Often one is enough:

no.value: Vi bør vel ringe dem først.

en.value: We should probably call them first, shouldn’t we?

no.value: Kanskje vi bør ringe dem først.

en.value: Perhaps we should call them first.

spans.value: Notice that the second example uses the accepted sentence-initial kanskje followed by subject–verb order: kanskje vi bør. It follows the same pattern as Kanskje vi kan låne et telt above.
Markers can also reveal different relationships to the same claim:

no.value: Konserten blir kanskje avlyst.

en.value: Perhaps the concert will be cancelled.

no.value: Konserten blir nok avlyst.

en.value: The concert will probably be cancelled.

no.value: Konserten blir visst avlyst.

en.value: Apparently, the concert is going to be cancelled.

no.value: Konserten blir vel avlyst?

en.value: The concert is going to be cancelled, I suppose?

no.value: Konserten blir jo avlyst.

en.value: The concert is being cancelled, as we both know.

spans.value: These are not interchangeable decorations. Each version positions the speaker differently toward the same event.
Checkpoint: changing only the stance

Take one basic statement about the concert, such as the expected attendance, the need for a tent, or the chance of cancellation. Recast it several times so that it becomes an open possibility, an inference, reported information, a shared assumption, and a tentative request for agreement.
Later that afternoon, Henrik calls the sports club. He then returns to Maja with an update.
Idrettslaget har visst et telt vi kan låne.

blocks.translation: Apparently, the sports club has a tent we can borrow.

spans.value: Så bra! Det er vel stort nok?

blocks.translation: That’s great! It is large enough, I suppose?

spans.value: Ja, det er sånn til tretti personer. Det holder nok.

blocks.translation: Yes, it is for something like thirty people. It will probably be enough.

spans.value: Vi bør kanskje hente det på fredag, hvis det passer for dem.

blocks.translation: Perhaps we should collect it on Friday, if that suits them.

spans.value: Enig. Vi må jo sette det opp før lydprøven.

blocks.translation: Agreed. After all, we have to put it up before the sound check.

spans.value: Jeg synes dette ble en mye bedre løsning.

blocks.translation: I think this turned into a much better solution.

spans.value: The second dialogue reuses the same forms, but the situation has moved forward. Henrik now has indirect information from the club, so visst is appropriate. Maja expects the tent to be large enough and invites confirmation with vel. Henrik gives an informal capacity with sånn and makes an inference with nok. Maja offers a softened proposal with kanskje, and Henrik supports it with shared scheduling knowledge marked by jo. Finally, Maja clearly labels her positive evaluation with synes.
Integrated practice: reconstructing the planning conversation

Create a short written exchange between Maja and Henrik after a new problem arises: the delivery van may be unavailable, another volunteer has heard that the sound equipment is delayed, and the walk from the car park takes about ten minutes. Keep the exchange focused on how certain each person is and where the information comes from.

Your exchange should distinguish possibility, inference, shared assumptions, reported information, personal opinion, and approximation. Avoid using every marker in every turn; each marker should have a clear reason to be present.

Do not use perhaps-level uncertainty when you mean reported information. Before correcting the example, recall that kanskje presents an open possibility, while visst indicates information heard or learned indirectly.
Correction task: A colleague has sent a message saying that Kari will come later, but a speaker says:

no.value: Kari kommer kanskje senere.

en.value: Perhaps Kari is coming later.

spans.value: Identify the contextual cue that makes the marker mismatched, replace the marker, and state how the repair changes the source or certainty meaning.

Without looking back, write a brief update from Henrik to a colleague about the concert. Include one uncertain possibility, one inference based on evidence, one piece of indirectly reported information, one reminder of shared knowledge, one tentative assumption seeking agreement, one personal opinion, and one approximate amount. Keep the update natural and connected rather than presenting separate example sentences. Your response should make the source and strength of each claim clear through the stance markers.

prompt.value: Værmelding: «Meteorologene er usikre på om været blir bedre før konserten.» Transportmelding: «Det er uavklart om bussen kommer før publikum.» Skriv en oppdatering til Maja. Presenter begge mulighetene som usikre, og bruk «kanskje» om hver av dem.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against criteria open-possibilities, both-updates, audience-purpose; report a verdict for each criterion and add no gating requirements.

criteria.instruction: Presents both outcomes as open possibilities and uses kanskje for each one.
Covers the weather and bus updates without presenting either outcome as established.
Functions as an update to Maja about the concert preparations.

prompt.value: Planleggingsnotat: «Det er uavklart om Henrik kan hente teltet.» Bilen hans står på verksted, og siste buss går før møtet er ferdig. Skriv en melding til Maja. Bruk «kanskje» om Henriks hjelp og «nok» om den sannsynlige transportløsningen.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against criteria possibility-with-kanskje, inference-with-nok, evidence-preserved, audience-purpose; report a verdict for each criterion and add no gating requirements.

criteria.instruction: Uses kanskje to present Henrik’s help as unresolved.
Uses nok for a likely transport conclusion supported by the stated evidence.
Keeps the unavailable car and early last bus relevant to the inference.
Functions as a planning message to Maja.

prompt.value: Melding fra en frivillig: «Lydutstyret er forsinket.» Ved lageret er porten låst og alle lysene slukket. Skriv en oppdatering til Maja. Formidle forsinkelsen med «visst» eller «visstnok», og trekk en sannsynlig slutning om lageret med «nok».

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against criteria indirect-report, evidence-inference, source-distinction, audience-purpose; report a verdict for each criterion and add no gating requirements.

criteria.instruction: Uses visst or visstnok to pass on the volunteer’s report about the delayed equipment.
Uses nok for a likely conclusion based on the locked gate and dark warehouse.
Keeps the indirect report distinct from the evidence-based inference.
Functions as an update to Maja.

prompt.value: Komiteen foreslår å flytte konserten til parkeringshuset. Det er billigere, men akustikken er dårlig. Svar komiteen. Skriv ditt personlige inntrykk med «synes» og standpunktet ditt med «mener» eller «etter min mening».

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against criteria personal-impression, considered-position, proposal-addressed, no-stacking, audience-purpose; report a verdict for each criterion and add no gating requirements.

criteria.instruction: Uses synes for a personal impression of the proposed venue.
Uses mener or etter min mening for a considered position about moving the concert.
Responds to the lower cost and weak acoustics in the supplied proposal.
Does not stack equivalent opinion frames without a separate communicative purpose.
Functions as a reply to the committee.

prompt.value: Planleggingstall: 180 publikummere, billettpris 400 kroner og ti minutters gange. I chatten står det at teltet rommer 30 personer og tar 5–10 minutter å sette opp. Skriv en oppdatering til planleggingsgruppa. Bruk nøytrale omtrentlige uttrykk for de tre første tallene og muntlig «sånn» for de to siste.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against criteria neutral-estimates, informal-estimates, figures-preserved, no-stacking, audience-purpose; report a verdict for each criterion and add no gating requirements.

criteria.instruction: Uses suitable neutral choices among rundt, omtrent, and cirka for the audience, ticket price, and walking time.
Uses sånn for the tent capacity and setup-time estimates.
Preserves all five supplied figures and their meanings.
Does not stack approximation markers without distinct purposes.
Functions as an update for the planning group.

prompt.value: Dere har avtalt at teltet skal være klart før lydprøven. Maja antar at det lånte teltet har plass til alle de frivillige. Skriv en melding til Henrik. Minn ham om avtalen med «jo», og be ham bekrefte teltkapasiteten med «vel».

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against criteria shared-reminder, tentative-confirmation, facts-preserved, audience-purpose; report a verdict for each criterion and add no gating requirements.

criteria.instruction: Uses jo to treat the previously agreed schedule as shared knowledge.
Uses vel in a question seeking confirmation of the tent capacity.
Keeps the sound-check deadline and unchecked capacity assumption distinct.
Functions as a message to Henrik.

prompt.value: Varebilen er kanskje ikke tilgjengelig. Nora sier at lydutstyret er forsinket. Parkeringsplassen er full, og det tar omtrent ti minutter å gå derfra. Maja og Henrik har avtalt å åpne portene tidlig. Skriv en samtale der de planlegger transport og rigging og blir enige om en løsning. Skill Noras beskjed fra egne antakelser, vis til avtalen, trekk en sannsynlig slutning om parkeringsplassen og ta med et personlig standpunkt.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against criteria supplied-facts, connected-decision, evidence-stance, car-park-inference, shared-agreement, personal-view, audience-purpose; report diagnostic verdicts for all ids ending in -observation without using them in the all-met pass rule. Valid variant that must pass: a connected exchange that covers every fact and reaches a workable decision and meets all stated criteria even if it uses different natural wording. Near-miss that must fail: unrelated example sentences that do not decide how to handle transport and setup. Accept natural wording without exact marker words, but fail a response that presents Nora’s report as mere speculation or a guess about the car park as something Nora reported.

criteria.instruction: Includes the possibly unavailable van, Nora’s report, the full car park, the approximate ten-minute walk, and the earlier agreement about opening the gates.
Forms one connected exchange that reaches a decision about transport and setup.
Keeps Nora’s report distinct from open possibilities and inferences; exact marker words are not required when the source and certainty are expressed naturally.
Draws a plausible, clearly inferential conclusion from the full car park about parking or transport; accepts natural wording without requiring nok.
Invokes the earlier gate-opening agreement as something both speakers already know.
Gives a participant’s own view of the best transport or setup plan, with natural opinion wording.
Uses dialogue appropriate to Maja and Henrik planning together.
Observe whether an open possibility is naturally marked, but do not fail the response on this criterion.
Observe whether the full car park supports a likely inference with nok, but do not fail the response on this criterion.
Observe whether Nora’s report is distinguished with visst or visstnok, but do not fail the response on this criterion.
Observe whether the earlier agreement is invoked with jo, but do not fail the response on this criterion.
Observe whether a personal view is framed with a taught opinion marker, but do not fail the response on this criterion.
Observe whether the walking time is marked as approximate, but do not fail the response on this criterion.

prompt.value: En kollega skriver: «Kari kommer kanskje senere.» Kontoret har hørt det fra en annen person, men kollegaen har ikke sjekket selv. Skriv setningen om for å vise at opplysningen kommer fra andre, og forklar kort hvordan betydningen endres.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate repaired-report and source-explanation as gating criteria. Accept natural Norwegian wording using visst or visstnok to mark an indirect report. Do not require a claim that Kari’s arrival has been independently confirmed.

criteria.instruction: Rewrites Kari’s arrival with visst or visstnok as indirectly reported information rather than an unsupported open possibility.
Explains that kanskje expresses a possibility while the repaired marker signals information heard or learned from another source.

prompt.value: Forhold på arrangementsområdet: Utescenen er kanskje fortsatt stengt. Vannpytter dekker de elektriske koblingene. Nora sier at nytt utstyr kommer klokka tolv. Henrik og kollegaen har avtalt å teste det før åpning. Det ventes rundt 180 publikummere. Skriv en oppdatering som hjelper kollegaen med morgenplanen. Skill Noras beskjed fra det som er usikkert, vis til avtalen, trekk en forsiktig slutning om koblingene, be kollegaen bekrefte én antakelse og gi ditt eget råd om planen.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against criteria facts-covered, useful-connected-update, evidence-based-inference, evidence-stance, shared-agreement, tentative-confirmation, personal-view, audience-purpose; report diagnostic verdicts for all ids ending in -observation without using them in the all-met pass rule. Valid variant that must pass: a coherent update covering all supplied facts and helping the colleague plan while meeting all stated criteria, regardless of exact marker choices. Near-miss that must fail: a list that omits Nora’s report and gives no usable morning plan. Accept natural wording without exact marker words, but fail an update that downgrades Nora’s stated report to a mere possibility.

criteria.instruction: Covers the stage uncertainty, wet electrical connections, Nora’s noon report, the testing agreement, and the approximate audience.
Connects the facts and inference into an update that helps the colleague plan the morning.

Draws a cautious inference from the puddles covering the electrical connections, such as that the connections may need inspection or drying before use; does not present this as a confirmed fact. Exact marker words are not required.
Attributes Nora’s noon report to Nora and distinguishes it from uncertain conditions and inferences; exact marker words are not required when source and certainty are clear.
Refers to the testing agreement as something the writer and colleague already settled.
Asks the colleague to confirm a tentative assumption about the morning plan, using natural wording; a suitable vel question is one option.
Gives the writer’s view of the best morning plan with natural opinion wording.
Functions as an update from Henrik to a colleague.
Observe whether the uncertain stage opening is marked with kanskje, but do not fail on this criterion.
Observe whether the puddles support an inference with nok, but do not fail on this criterion.
Observe whether Nora’s report is marked with visst or visstnok, but do not fail on this criterion.
Observe whether the testing agreement is invoked with jo, but do not fail on this criterion.
Observe whether any tentative request for confirmation uses vel naturally, but do not fail on this criterion.
Observe whether a personal judgment uses a taught opinion frame, but do not fail on this criterion.
Observe whether the audience figure is appropriately approximate, but do not fail on this criterion.

prompt.value: Velg svaret som lar utfallet stå åpent.

explanation.value: «Kanskje» viser til en åpen mulighet. «Nok» framstiller et utfall som sannsynlig.

options.text: Det regner kanskje på lørdag.
options.why: Kanskje leaves rain as one unresolved possibility.

options.text: Det regner nok på lørdag.
options.why: Nok presents rain as the speaker’s likely conclusion, which is stronger than the note supports.

options.text: Det regner visst på lørdag.
options.why: Visst presents the claim as indirectly reported rather than merely possible.

stem.value: Værmelding: «Regn er mulig, men varselet er usikkert.»

prompt.value: Velg setningen som uttrykker en åpen mulighet om å flytte konserten inn. Arrangørene har ikke bestemt seg.

explanation.value: «Kanskje» passer til en uavklart plan. «Nok» presenterer en sannsynlig slutning, og «visst» antyder en indirekte beskjed.

options.text: Konserten blir kanskje flyttet inn.
options.why: «Kanskje» lar flytting være en åpen mulighet uten å si at den er sannsynlig.

options.text: Konserten blir nok flyttet inn.
options.why: Kraftig regn og mørke skyer kan støtte denne sannsynlige slutningen, men «nok» uttrykker ikke en åpen mulighet.

options.text: Konserten blir visst flyttet inn.
options.why: «Visst» antyder en indirekte beskjed, men ingen slik beskjed er nevnt.

stem.value: Værmeldingen varsler kraftig regn, og mørke skyer samler seg. Arrangørene har ikke bestemt seg for om konserten skal flyttes inn.

prompt.value: Velg svaret som formidler beskjeden.

explanation.value: «Visst» eller «visstnok» passer når opplysningen kommer fra en annen kilde.

options.text: Lydutstyret kommer visst etter klokka seks.
options.why: Visst marks the volunteer’s message as the indirect source.

options.text: Lydutstyret kommer kanskje etter klokka seks.
options.why: Kanskje makes the delay an open possibility and loses the reported-source meaning.

options.text: Lydutstyret kommer nok etter klokka seks.
options.why: Nok presents a likely inference rather than information passed on from the volunteer.

stem.value: Melding fra frivillig: «Lydutstyret blir levert etter klokka seks.»

prompt.value: Velg formuleringen som tydeligst viser at opplysningen kommer fra varselet, uten å fremstille den som helt sikker.

explanation.value: «Visst» gir en opplysning fra en annen kilde videre. «Nok» markerer en egen sannsynlig slutning, og «kanskje» en åpen mulighet.

options.text: Veien er visst stengt.
options.why: Visst presents the closure as indirectly reported information from the notice.

options.text: Veien er nok stengt.
options.why: «Nok» markerer først og fremst talerens egen slutning, ikke at opplysningen kommer fra varselet.

options.text: Veien er kanskje stengt.
options.why: «Kanskje» viser en åpen mulighet, men sier ikke at opplysningen kommer fra varselet.

stem.value: Et nettvarsel fra veimyndigheten sier at adkomstveien er stengt. Det er mulig at varselet ikke er oppdatert.

prompt.value: Velg svaret som passer til kilden.

explanation.value: «Visst» viser til en opplysning fra en annen kilde. «Nok» uttrykker en sannsynlig slutning.

options.text: Idrettslaget har visst et telt vi kan låne.
options.why: Visst passes on information received from the club worker.

options.text: Idrettslaget har nok et telt vi kan låne.
options.why: Nok would make the tent a likely inference rather than a reported fact.

stem.value: Melding fra en i klubben: «Vi har et telt dere kan låne.»

prompt.value: Velg svaret som uttrykker en sannsynlig slutning ut fra klubbens tidligere utlån.

explanation.value: «Nok» uttrykker en sannsynlig slutning ut fra tidligere utlån. «Visst» ville signalisert en opplysning fra en annen kilde.

options.text: Idrettslaget har nok et telt vi kan låne.
options.why: Nok presents a likely conclusion based on the club’s repeated past lending.

options.text: Idrettslaget har visst et telt vi kan låne.
options.why: Visst suggests indirectly reported information, but no report has been received.

stem.value: Klubben har lånt ut telt til Maja og Henrik ved de fem siste utendørskonsertene. De planlegger en ny konsert, men har ikke spurt klubben ennå.

prompt.value: Velg svaret som viser alle formuleringene som kan uttrykke Majas personlige inntrykk.

explanation.value: «Synes» innleder ofte et personlig inntrykk. «Mener» uttrykker ofte en gjennomtenkt holdning.

options.text: Både «Jeg synes lokalet er hyggelig» og «Jeg mener at lokalet er hyggelig».
options.why: Begge formuleringene kan uttrykke Majas personlige inntrykk.

options.text: Lokalet er visst hyggelig.
options.why: «Visst» gjør vurderingen til en indirekte gjengitt opplysning.

stem.value: Maja forteller om inntrykket sitt av lokalet.

prompt.value: Velg svaret som uttrykker komiteens standpunkt og begrunner det med utgiftene til vakthold.

explanation.value: «Mener» innleder et gjennomtenkt standpunkt. Den konkrete begrunnelsen gjør standpunktet etterprøvbart.

options.text: Komiteen mener at kommunen bør støtte arrangementet fordi bidraget kan betale for en vekter som arrangørene ikke har råd til.
options.why: Mener presents the committee’s considered position, and the stated reason supports the request for municipal funding.

options.text: Komiteen tror kommunen vil støtte arrangementet, fordi bidraget kan betale for en vekter som arrangørene ikke har råd til.
options.why: Tro expresses uncertainty about a factual outcome, not the committee’s argued position.

options.text: Etter min mening mener komiteen at kommunen bør støtte arrangementet, fordi bidraget kan betale for en vekter som arrangørene ikke har råd til.
options.why: The two opinion frames are stacked without a separate function, even though the reason is present.

stem.value: Henrik uttaler seg på vegne av komiteen og argumenterer for kommunal støtte. Begrunnelsen er at bidraget kan betale for en vekter som arrangørene ikke har råd til.

prompt.value: Velg formuleringen som passer til notatets stil.

explanation.value: «Rundt», «omtrent» og «cirka» er nøytrale. «Sånn» er muntlig og omtrentlig.

options.text: Budsjettet er på omtrent 80 000 kroner.
options.why: Omtrent gives a neutral approximation suited to a planning note.

options.text: Budsjettet er på sånn 80 000 kroner.
options.why: Sånn is deliberately conversational and too loose for the stated document.

options.text: Budsjettet er på sånn cirka rundt 80 000 kroner.
options.why: The approximation markers are needlessly stacked.

prompt.value: Velg det naturlige, muntlige overslaget.

explanation.value: «Sånn» passer til et omtrentlig overslag i en uformell samtale.

options.text: Det er sånn til tretti personer.
options.why: Sånn gives the deliberately rough conversational estimate requested.

options.text: Det er til tretti personer.
options.why: Without an approximation marker, the capacity sounds exact.

options.text: Det er sånn omtrent rundt tretti personer.
options.why: Several approximation markers are stacked without separate functions.

stem.value: Henrik snakker uformelt med Maja om et telt merket for 28–32 personer.

prompt.value: Velg påminnelsen som viser at dette allerede er avtalt.

explanation.value: «Jo» viser til noe taleren regner som felles kjent. «Vel» åpner ofte for at lytteren bekrefter antakelsen.

options.text: Vi må jo sette opp teltet før lydprøven.
options.why: Jo presents the schedule as already shared or accepted.

options.text: Vi må vel sette opp teltet før lydprøven?
options.why: Vel asks for tentative confirmation instead of simply invoking shared knowledge.

options.text: Vi må kanskje sette opp teltet før lydprøven.
options.why: Kanskje makes the requirement uncertain.

stem.value: Maja og Henrik har avtalt at teltet skal være reist før lydprøven.

prompt.value: Velg det naturlige spørsmålet fra Maja.

explanation.value: «Vel» passer når taleren antar noe forsiktig og ber lytteren bekrefte det.

options.text: Det er vel stort nok?
options.why: Vel marks a tentative assumption and invites Henrik’s confirmation.

options.text: Det er jo stort nok.
options.why: Jo treats the size as shared or obvious and does not genuinely seek confirmation.

options.text: Det er nok stort nok.
options.why: Nok gives Maja’s likely assessment but does not specifically invite agreement.

stem.value: Maja tror det lånte teltet er stort nok, men Henrik har målene og hun vil gjerne ha det bekreftet.

prompt.value: Det er ikke avgjort om konserten skal flyttes inn. Fullfør setningen: «Vi flytter ___ konserten inn.»
